'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***The [[Houthi movement]] [[piracy|hijacks]] the British [[cargo ship]] ''{{ill|Galaxy Leader|ru|Захват Galaxy Leader}}'' operated by a [[Japan]]ese company and partially owned by an [[Israel]]i businessman in the [[Red Sea]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2023/11/19/Israeli-ship-reportedly-hijacked-by-Yemen-s-Houthis-in-Red-Sea (Al Arabiya)] [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-774045 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***The [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]] shells [[Russia]]n-occupied [[Kalmiuske Raion]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], striking a [[dance hall]] in Kumachove during a performance, killing about 20 [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian troops]] and Russian actress [[List of entertainers who died during a performance#21st century|Polina Menshikh]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-67495384 (BBC News)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**At least 32 people are killed and 20 others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] against two villages in [[Abyei]], an area that is [[territorial dispute|disputed]] between [[Sudan]] and [[South Sudan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-sudan-sudan-abyei-un-peacekeepers-16f01174aee98709c98d504696db8159 (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*One of [[Emperor of the French|French emperor]] [[Napoleon]]'s [[bicorne]] hats is sold for a record {{Euro|1.93 million|link=yes}} (around [[United States dollar|US$]]2.11 million) at an [[auction]] in [[France]]. [https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/napoleons-hat-sells-for-record-sum-at-french-auction/article_b1866578-a5c6-529c-b87c-21e3debd03d8.html (AFP via KPVI)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Optus]] [[CEO]] Kelly Bayer Rosmarin [[resign]]s following a [[2023 Optus outage|network outage]] in [[Australia]] that took down its phone and [[internet service]]s nationwide for 14 hours earlier this month. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/nov/20/optus-ceo-kelly-bayer-rosmarin-resigns-network-outage-australia?fbclid=IwAR3yKNTKrk5xHB2bOUC0ZzH-e77iQReW-AjFz99K_PuHKaCOxUoVvqywTv4 (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Africa floods]]
**The death toll from the [[flood]]s in [[Kenya]], [[Somalia]], and [[Ethiopia]], increases to 130 people. The Somali town of [[Beledweyne]] has been completely submerged after the [[Shebelle River]] burst its banks, forcing 90% of the population out of their homes, while 30,000 people are [[internally displaced person|displaced]] in Kenya as hundreds of homes have been destroyed. [https://apnews.com/article/kenya-somalia-ethiopia-south-sudan-4f42266e594c1d6b6e1f464c0a83df27 (AP)]
*At least 21 people are killed by flooding in the [[Dominican Republic]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/dominican-republic-alert-after-deadly-floods-kill-least-nine-2023-11-19/ (Reuters)]
*Eleven people are killed when a [[Kereta Api Indonesia|passenger train]] [[list of level crossing crashes|hits]] their minibus on a no-barrier [[level crossing]] in [[Lumajang]], [[East Java]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2023/11/20/11-killed-in-train-minibus-collision-in-indonesia039s-east-java (Xinhua via ''The Star'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Myanmar relations]]
**Pro-[[State Administration Council|military junta]] nationalists stage protests against [[China]] outside the Chinese embassy and [[Yangon City Hall]] in [[Yangon]], [[Myanmar]], accusing the [[Government of China|Chinese government]] of secretly backing [[Three Brotherhood Alliance|rebel forces]] in [[Shan State]]. [https://www.irrawaddy.com/specials/myanmar-china-watch/myanmar-regime-backed-rallies-denounce-china-accusing-it-of-backing-anti-junta-alliance.html (Irrawaddy)]
*[[Nicaragua]] completes its withdrawal from the [[Organization of American States]]. [https://www.laprensalatina.com/the-history-behind-nicaraguas-exit-from-the-oas/ (''La Prensa Latina'')] [https://www.laprensani.com/2023/11/19/politica/3239520-a-partir-de-este-domingo-nicaragua-esta-oficialmente-fuera-de-la-oea (''La Prensa'')] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Argentine general election]]
**[[Javier Milei]] of [[La Libertad Avanza]] is elected [[President of Argentina|president]] after beating [[Peronism|Peronist]] [[Sergio Massa]] 56% to 44% in the [[Run-off election|second round run-off]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-67470549 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 ATP Tour]]
**[[2023 ATP Finals]]
***In [[tennis]], [[Sport in Serbia|Serbian]] [[Novak Djokovic]] wins a record seventh [[ATP Finals]] [[2023 ATP Finals – Singles|singles title]] after defeating [[Tennis in Italy|Italian]] [[Jannik Sinner]] in two [[Set (tennis)|sets]], 6–3, 6–3, in the final. Djokovic, who successfully [[2022 ATP Finals – Singles|defended]] his title, surpasses [[Roger Federer]]'s total of six titles. [https://apnews.com/article/djokovic-record-sinner-atp-finals-turin-e17000d7eb251bf962989edff8c984e1 (AP)]
*[[2023 CFL season]]
**[[110th Grey Cup]]
***In [[Canadian football]], the [[Montreal Alouettes]] defeat the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] 28–24, claiming their eighth [[Canadian Football League]] [[Grey Cup|championship]] title. [https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/montreal-alouettes-rally-to-beat-winnipeg-blue-bombers-to-take-grey-cup-1.2038100 (TSN)]
*[[2023 Cricket World Cup]]
**In [[cricket]], [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] wins a [[List of Cricket World Cup records|record]] sixth [[Cricket World Cup|World Cup]] title after defeating host nation [[India national cricket team|India]] by six [[wicket]]s in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup final|final]]. India's [[Virat Kohli]] is named [[Cricket World Cup awards#Player of the tournament|player of the tournament]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231119-starc-takes-three-as-australia-bowl-out-india-for-240-in-world-cup-final (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2023 League of Legends World Championship|2023 ''League of Legends'' World Championship]]
**In [[esports]], [[Sport in South Korea|South Korea]]n team [[T1 (esports)|T1]] wins a record-extending fourth [[League of Legends World Championship|World Championship]] in the [[multiplayer online battle arena]] video game ''[[League of Legends]]'', after defeating [[Sport in China|Chinese]] team [[Weibo Gaming]] 3–0 in the final. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231119-south-korea-s-t1-win-record-fourth-league-of-legends-world-title (AFP via France 24)]
